about: How a finished video is filed in the archive. Krish, 2026-10-06: "Can you ensure all videos are always archived properly in folder with date/subject/where I can post it in the folder name?"

Two programs follow this rule: the Studio (packages/core/src/archive-naming.ts) and quick-edit (scripts/quick-edit/archive.py). Both are tested against every case in this file, so they cannot drift apart. Change the rule here first, then in both programs.
Folder: YYYY-MM-DD <Subject> (post to <Where>). Files: <Subject> - tall 9x16 - <Where>.mp4 and <Subject> - wide 16x9 - <Where>.mp4.
Date: the piece's publish date when known, else the day it was archived on Krish's clock (time_zone).
Where: the places the files are for, always in the order of places, joined with a comma and a space. A name is matched whatever its capitals.

Safe on Windows and Google Drive: every control character and every kind of space becomes a plain space, the characters < > : " / \ | ? * are removed, runs of spaces become one, and spaces and dots at either end are removed (dots only at the end).

At most folder_max characters (counted as Unicode code points) in a folder name. Only the subject is shortened: it is cut at the last space that fits (or mid-word when one word is too long), and spaces, dots, commas, semicolons and dashes left at its end are removed. The date and the where list are never shortened.
When the folder already exists (capitals ignored, as on Windows and Drive), the name gets " (2)", then " (3)" and so on, still inside folder_max. Nothing is ever overwritten.
